verdict.root_cause: The ad service is itself emitting gRPC UNAVAILABLE on a minority of GetAds calls. Its error ratio rose roughly tenfold (0.36% baseline to ~3.5% mean, peaking ~9.2%) with onset inside the window and repeated change points early, mid and late [tr_5493ede46fc2]. ad's own log shows UNAVAILABLE returned from GetAds with no description and no cause, no stack trace, no startup or shutdown banner, and normal request handling on either side of each failure [tr_055e2616619a]. Traces show ad as a leaf with only sub-millisecond in-process children and no outbound call that could be propagating the error [tr_32512397a410], and flagd is healthy with an error ratio an order of magnitude too small to supply ad's errors [tr_1d8eb3120f7a]. No deployment, image-tag, resource or config edit is recorded for ad or flagd [tr_3b02d59b7496][tr_97c92d0d93b7]. A runtime-gated failure path inside ad — a flag toggled in the flag store, which leaves no change-log entry — fits all of this: in-process, partial, abrupt, attached to no artifact or file change.
verdict.reasoning: The error is generated by ad, not received by it: ad logs the UNAVAILABLE status itself with a null cause and no exception, and every sampled ad span is a leaf with no outbound child [tr_055e2616619a][tr_32512397a410]. The failure is partial and recurrent, not total or progressive — under ~10% error ratio with successes interleaved — which excludes a hard outage, a crash-restart loop (continuous logging, no init lines) and a slow-dependency cascade (internal ops finish in 0.0–0.3ms, nowhere near a deadline) [tr_5493ede46fc2][tr_055e2616619a]. Meanwhile nothing was deployed or edited [tr_3b02d59b7496][tr_97c92d0d93b7] and the flag service itself is serving normally [tr_1d8eb3120f7a]. A healthy flag store plus an empty change log plus a brand-new in-process failure path in its consumer is the signature of a flipped flag: the flagged code path fails while the store holding the flag is fine. The fix is reverting the flag value, not rolling back an artifact that never changed.
open_questions: The flag store was never queried — the specific flag, its value and its change time are inferred from the failure's shape, not observed.
Both change-history queries ran from the incident timestamp forward ~24h, so the hours before 20:41:16 were never examined; a pre-onset change would not appear [tr_3b02d59b7496][tr_97c92d0d93b7].

No trace falls inside 20:41–20:43 and all sampled traces succeeded [tr_32512397a410], so the absence of an outbound span is established only for successful requests; frontend logs returned no message bodies [tr_26d463c9ea8a], leaving caller-side impact and the other two affected services uncharacterised.

alternatives.root_cause: A change to ad landed before 20:41:16, outside the queried window, putting a faulty build or setting into service that fails a fraction of requests.
alternatives.why_not: Cannot be excluded on change data given the window mis-scope, but ad's log shows no startup banner or process interruption anywhere in the window [tr_055e2616619a], and a pre-window deploy does not explain onset sharply inside the window after a near-zero baseline [tr_5493ede46fc2].

alternatives.root_cause: An unobserved dependency of ad began refusing connections and ad surfaces that to callers as UNAVAILABLE.
alternatives.why_not: No outbound span from ad appears in any of 132 sampled spans and no call-path waiting is visible [tr_32512397a410]; failures are instant rather than slow, which is the opposite of a latency-driven mechanism.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is predicted. What should happen next is an observation, not a change: query the flag store directly for ad-related flags (e.g. the ad-service failure/error gate) and their current values and last-modified times, and re-run the change-history queries over the window *before* 2026-10-09T20:41:16 rather than forward from it. If a flag is found enabled, the error-ratio series sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="ad",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m]))/sum(rate(...)) would be the measurement that confirms a subsequent revert worked, falling from ~3.5% mean back toward the 0.36% baseline within two 5m windows.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the flag store query comes back showing a prior recorded configuration for ad with an ad-side failure flag toggled on inside the window — that would satisfy both preconditions of revert_config and make the abstention an avoidable delay. It is also wrong if ad's error ratio climbs past the ~9.2% peak toward total failure, in which case waiting for evidence costs more than acting on a medium-confidence guess. Conversely, if errors subside on their own with no intervention, the abstention was correct and the fault was transient.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued intermittent ~3.5% GetAds failures (peaking ~9.2%) for as long as it takes to query the flag store — user-visible ad failures on the storefront, unresolved. The risk of the alternative I am declining, revert_config on ad, is concrete: ad's change history is empty [tr_3b02d59b7496], so there is no recorded prior configuration to restore. The executor would either refuse or restore some default that was never the running config, changing environment values (dependency addresses, flag-source pointers) that are currently correct, and recreating the container. That could convert a 3.5% partial failure into a full outage of ad, and the diagnosis that motivates it — a specific flag with a specific value — was never observed, only inferred from the failure's shape. restart_service is also wrong here: the logs rule out a crash, restart or in-process exception [tr_055e2616619a], the evidence points at a runtime-gated code path rather than corrupted process state, and a flag held in an external store survives a container recreate, so the restart would discard cache and buy nothing.
proposal.blast_radius: Abstaining changes nothing, so nobody sees a new effect; frontend and frontend-proxy continue to see the existing minority of failed GetAds calls propagating up from ad, with caller-side impact still uncharacterised because frontend logs returned no message bodies. Had I proposed revert_config or restart_service on ad, the blast radius would have been ad plus its inbound callers — frontend directly, and frontend-proxy and end users behind it — who would see connection resets for the duration of the container recreate, on top of the errors already occurring.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A critical alert on ad with no open incidents to absorb it cannot be dismissed. flagd as the immediate upstream dependency makes a flag/config change a cheap first guess, nothing more.
